dimensions.evidence: train and provide resources for first responders and members of other relevant community sectors on carrying and facilitating access to fentanyl or xylazine test strips

dimensions.assessment: Broadens allowable grant activities and establishes new federal guidance and study requirements regarding harm reduction tools.
dimensions.evidence: authorize the use of grant funds for such test strips

dimensions.assessment: Permits existing grant funds to be used for new items and requires federal agencies to conduct a study, though no new total funding authorization amount is specified.
dimensions.evidence: authorize the use of grant funds for such test strips

dimensions.assessment: Modifies Public Health Service Act grant programs, directs multiple executive agencies to build research frameworks, and mandates a federal study.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of Health and Human Services, in consultation with the Director of the National Institutes of Health... shall develop and make publicly available research and marketing frameworks

dimensions.assessment: Ongoing programmatic expansion with a specific two-year deadline for the required study report.
dimensions.evidence: not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, submit to Congress a report on the study conducted

importance_detail.rationale: Expands federal first-responder grant uses to include rapid test strips for synthetic opioids, directs federal agencies to establish research and marketing frameworks, and mandates a study and congressional report.
